{{Infobox football league season | competition = [[Chinese Super League]] | season = 2005 | winners = [[Dalian Shide F.C.|Dalian Shide]] (8th title) | relegated = N/A | continentalcup1 = [[2006 AFC Champions League|AFC Champions League]] | continentalcup1 qualifiers = {{ubl|[[Dalian Shide F.C.|Dalian Shide]] | [[Shanghai Shenhua F.C.|Shanghai Shenhua]]}} | continentalcup2 = [[2006 A3 Champions Cup|A3 Champions Cup]] | continentalcup2 qualifiers = [[Dalian Shide F.C.|Dalian Shide]] | league topscorer = [[Branko Jelić]] (21 goals) | matches = 182 | total goals = 465 | average attendance = 10,284 | prevseason = [[2004 Chinese Super League|2004]] | nextseason = [[2006 Chinese Super League|2006]] }} The '''2005 Chinese Super League''' season was the second season of [[China]]'s top-tier [[Association football|football]] competition. With no relegation the previous season, the league expanded from 12 to 14 clubs with the promotion of [[Shanghai United F.C.|Shanghai United]] and [[Wuhan Optics Valley F.C.|Wuhan Huanghelou]]. The season was scheduled to start on 5 March 2005, but was postponed until April due to a sponsorship problem and finished on 5 November with [[Dalian Shide F.C.|Dalian Shide]], seven-time champions in the old first division, clinching their eighth title. Defending champions [[Shenzhen F.C.|Shenzhen Jianlibao]] finished third from bottom, the second consecutive year in which the defending champions has done so. The FA had announced at the start of the season that no teams would be relegated for this season and they kept to this decision. ==Promotion and relegation== '''Teams promoted from [[2004 China League One]]''' *[[Wuhan Optics Valley F.C.|Wuhan Huanghelou]] *[[Shanghai United F.C.|Shanghai United]] '''Teams relegated after end of [[2004 Chinese Super League]]''' *None ==Season review== The two-year-old league provided a more positive side of football than the previous season, with much fewer drug-abusing, match-fixing and other scandals on and off the pitch. However, the season was criticised for being unexciting with some stating that the only reason that particular clubs did well was because of foreign talents. Most teams had not invested enough into their squads for the season to compete for the top positions in the CSL. As the decision to cancel relegation had been announced before the start of the season, unlike the previous season where it was decided halfway through. Teams with no chance of winning the league were thus reluctant to spend money in the transfer market. Nevertheless, there was still strong competition at the top of the table with six teams fighting for the top two [[AFC Champions League Elite|AFC Champions League]] spots. [[Dalian Shide F.C.|Dalian Shide]] remained at the top for almost the whole length of the season but there was a constant rotation of second place. At the lower half of the table, [[Chongqing Liangjiang Athletic F.C.|Chongqing Lifan]] finished at the bottom of the table for two years running while [[Guangzhou City F.C.|Shenyang Ginde]] deteriorated to second from bottom. ===Early surprises=== Among the contenders for the second spot, [[Wuhan Optics Valley F.C.|Wuhan Huanghelou]] was no doubt the surprise package. The team, promoted to the CSL the previous season, was little known to their opponents; but they started superbly, embarking on a seven match winning streak at one point, which put them hot on the heels of Dalian Shide. However, like many inexperienced sides, their composure failed in the second half of the season but they still finished a remarkable fifth. ===Late dash=== In the second half of the season, the battle for second was mainly between [[Shanghai Shenhua F.C.|Shanghai Shenhua]] and [[Tianjin Jinmen Tiger F.C.|Tianjin TEDA]]. The gap between the two clubs was tiny and neither could afford slip-ups, although [[Shandong Taishan F.C.|Shandong Luneng]] and [[Beijing Guoan F.C.|Beijing Hyundai]], who were also within striking distance, were eyeing their opponents' performances closely. Shanghai Shenhua had a late surge of form to secure second with Shandong Luneng finished third to miss the final ACL spot by just one point while Tianjin TEDA was happy enough with a fourth place. Dalian Shide won their eighth top-tier title with a 12 points cushion although they and Shanghai Shenhua had lost the same number of games because they had managed to win 6 games more. ==Personnel== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size:95%" |- !Team !Manager |- | [[Beijing Guoan F.C.|Beijing Hyundai]] | {{flagicon|China}} [[Shen Xiangfu]] |- | [[Chongqing Liangjiang Athletic F.C.|Chongqing Lifan]] | {{Flagicon|CHN}} [[Ma Lin (footballer)|Ma Lin]] |- | [[Dalian Shide F.C.|Dalian Shide]] | {{flagicon|Serbia and Montenegro}} [[Vladimir Petrović]] |- | [[Beijing Chengfeng F.C.|Inter Shanghai]] | {{flagicon|China}} [[Cheng Yaodong]] |- | [[Liaoning F.C.|Liaoning Zhongyu]] | {{flagicon|China}} [[Tang Yaodong]] |- | [[Qingdao Hainiu F.C.|Qingdao Zhongneng]] | {{flagicon|China}} [[Yin Tiesheng]] |- | [[Shandong Taishan F.C.|Shandong Luneng]] | {{flagicon|Serbia and Montenegro}} [[Ljubiša Tumbaković]] |- | [[Shanghai Shenhua F.C.|Shanghai Shenhua]] | {{flagicon|Russia}} [[Valery Nepomnyashchy]] |- | [[Shanghai United F.C.|Shanghai United]] | |- | [[Guangzhou City F.C.|Shenyang Ginde]] | {{flagicon|England}} [[Bob Houghton]] |- | [[Shenzhen F.C.|Shenzhen Jianlibao]] | {{flagicon|China}} [[Guo Ruilong]] |- | [[Sichuan First City F.C.|Sichuan Guangdong]] | {{flagicon|China}} [[Gao Huichen]] |- | [[Tianjin Jinmen Tiger F.C.|Tianjin TEDA]] | {{flagicon|China}} [[Liu Chunming]] |- | [[Wuhan Optics Valley F.C.|Wuhan Huanghelou]] | {{flagicon|China}} [[Chen Fangping]] |} ==Foreign players== The number of foreign players is restricted to three, but all teams can only use two foreign players on the field in each game.
